forms.description: Every named form of this spell, e.g. Comet, Comet - Charged, Comet - Charged (AoE). They have different attack values; this result covers only the one named.

spell_buff.description: The catalyst's spell buff, the figure the game shows on it. Carries all the stat scaling.

base_attack.description: The spell's own attack per damage type, before the catalyst. A sorcery is normally magic and an incantation fire, lightning or holy.

damage_types.description: The types this spell actually deals. Quote it: 'Black Flame does 1013 fire' is an answer, '1013' is not.

bonus.description: The catalyst's family multiplier, or 1.0 when none applies.

bonus_family.description: The family the bonus was applied for, empty when none was.

family_source.description: Where the family membership came from, when a bonus was applied. Not the Build Planner: say so if it matters.

attack.description: The whole spell: every type's base_attack x spell_buff / 100 x bonus, added up.

attack_shown.description: The same figure truncated, as displayed.

attack_by_type.description: Where that total comes from. A spell that deals two types is two figures and one of them is what a resistant enemy takes.

attack_shown_by_type.description: The same figures truncated, as displayed.

fp_cost.description: The spell's own FP cost, before the catalyst.

castable.description: Whether the build meets every requirement. False means the spell cannot be cast at all — not that it is weaker.

catalyst_casts.description: What this catalyst can cast, from the game's own enableMagic / enableMiracle flags: Sorcery, Incantation, or both — the Staff of the Great Beyond casts both.

catalyst_can_cast_this.description: Whether this catalyst can cast this spell at all. False makes every figure here about a cast that cannot happen.

fp_cost_actual.description: What it costs out of this catalyst, rounded up. Lusat's charges 1.5x for its spell buff and Azur's 1.2x; quote this one when comparing catalysts.

fp_rate.description: The catalyst's FP multiplier, 1.0 for all but two staves.

starting_class.description: The class this was computed as. It is not cosmetic: planner.py treats a class's stats as a floor, so a Wretch's flat tens lift any stat below 10.

stats_used.description: The stats the figure was actually computed at, after the class floor.

stats_raised_by_class.description: Stats the class lifted above what was asked for. Non-empty means this figure is for a slightly different character, and an answer has to say so.
